ops.title: Flaky golden: test_codex_ask_foreground_lane_reuse_serializes fails ~1 in 5 at HEAD
ops.description:
`plugins/repo-bootstrap/tests/test_scaffold.py::test_codex_ask_foreground_lane_reuse_serializes` is intermittently red. Measured 2026-07-25 against a clean `git worktree` at HEAD (no local changes, no shim fix): 1 failure in 5 isolated runs. Re-measured on a working tree carrying the binrun plugin-root fix: 1 failure in 3 isolated runs. It also passed repeatedly under `pytest -k codex_ask`, which is what made it look at first like an ordering artifact or a mid-edit tree — it is neither. Pre-existing and independent of the changes in flight.

Failure mode as first observed: the replacement same-lane call exits 1 with `lane busy; --await it or mint a new lane` instead of blocking until the first run exits (the serialization the test asserts around test_scaffold.py:1398-1403).

Why it matters beyond noise: codex CI runs the full golden suite on every push to `plugins/codex/**`, so this reds pushes at random and trains readers to re-run rather than read. A flaky test in the lane-reuse path also masks exactly the class of defect being fixed right now.

Likely not independent of the confirmed lock findings in task 81486106 — specifically finding 4 (prune does terminal reclassification and RemoveAll with no lock while dispatch republishes meta under the exclusive lock) and the busy-lane check in dispatch.go, which treats a meta newer than 5s with no pid as a live launch window. A timing-dependent verdict there is the obvious suspect for a timing-dependent test failure. Diagnose alongside that work rather than as an isolated test-stability patch; if the fix makes lane reuse deterministic the flake should disappear on its own, and if it does not, the test's own assumption needs re-examining.

ops.text: The failure is root-caused to either the test's timing assumption or a real race in lane reuse, with the mechanism named
The test passes 20 consecutive isolated runs after the fix
Any production-code race found is fixed rather than papered over by loosening the assertion
